## 固定收益開篇論點

美國公債7月1日收盤時，前端變動不大，較長天期債券則溫和走弱。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh承認通膨風險已下降，但美國製造業與就業數據仍具韌性，兩股力量相互拉鋸。2年期殖利率上升0.2個基點至4.177%，5年期上升1.1個基點至4.238%，10年期上升1.4個基點至4.48%，30年期則上升1.8個基點至4.971%。殖利率曲線小幅陡峭化，2年與10年期利差擴大1.2個基點至30.3個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大1.6個基點至79.4個基點。

這波溫和賣壓集中在實質利率，而非通膨補償。10年期實質殖利率上升1.7個基點至2.243%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降0.3個基點至2.237%。這種組合反映經濟仍在擴張、聯準會也不願預先承諾政策路徑；即使油價與投入成本下降，降低了眼前的通膨威脅，實質利率仍居高不下。Warsh表示，過去四週通膨預期與風險均已下降，一度帶動2年期殖利率回落至約4.15%，但他拒絕說明7月是否仍可能升息。

製造業連續第六個月擴張，民間就業也再度穩健增加。供應管理協會的價格指標則創2022年7月以來最大單月跌幅，就業分項雖有改善，仍略低於擴張門檻。紐約聯準銀行的一項勞動市場緊俏指標亦顯示，薪資成長接近但略低於長期常態。綜合來看，這些數據支持經濟持續成長，卻未重新出現聯準會6月會議後一度推升升息預期的強烈通膨訊號。

能源市場進一步強化了這項區別。美國官員稱與伊朗的間接磋商具有建設性後，WTI下跌1.32%至$68.58，布蘭特原油下跌1.85%至$71.57。商業原油與汽油庫存雖然下降，但市場價格走低，加上餾分油庫存增加，使通膨訊號保持溫和。WTI與布蘭特原油一個月跌幅均超過21%；即使美國與伊朗之間的安排能否持久仍不確定，這種幅度的逆轉已足以影響整體通膨及央行假設。

風險市場並未呈現與利率走勢相對應的典型格局。標普500指數下跌0.22%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.54%，費城半導體指數更重挫6.27%，美國公債卻未上漲，顯示晶片股賣壓沒有演變成廣泛的避險潮。美元指數上升0.20%至101.39，上市投資級、高收益及新興市場債券基金則全數下跌。因此，當日最鮮明的特徵不是通膨衝擊再起，也不是全面性的信用事件，而是投資人在物價訊號轉弱、經濟活動具韌性、聯準會減少政策指引，以及資本密集型科技企業債務供給增加之間權衡之際，實質殖利率持續處於高檔。

## Warsh降溫通膨疑慮，但未為7月會議定調

Warsh在辛特拉發表談話後，7月升息的急迫性降低，但政策決定仍未明朗。他表示，近幾週通膨預期與通膨風險已下降，並重申聯準會致力讓通膨回到2%。政策敏感端的市場反應最為明顯：2年期美國公債殖利率在談話後降至約4.15%的盤中低點，7月1日收於4.177%，較前一交易日幾乎沒有變化。

Warsh沒有說明這項評估所依據的物價指標。聯準會偏好的最新通膨指標年增率仍為4.1%，核心指標為3.4%；不過，隨著美國與伊朗和平努力取得進展，原油與汽油價格均已大幅下跌。因此，他的談話承認近期通膨環境已有重要改善，卻沒有宣稱更廣泛的物價壓力已回到目標。

對於7月28日至29日會議是否可能升息，Warsh同樣不願表態。他重申，聯準會將停止提供讓市場預先鎖定預期利率路徑的前瞻指引，並表示決策官員屆時將進行實質討論。FOMC在6月一致決議將聯邦資金利率目標維持於3.50%至3.75%；提交預測的18名官員中，有一半預期2026年會升息，Warsh則是唯一未提交利率預測的官員。

溝通方式的改變，將提高每項新數據撼動殖利率曲線前端的能力。利率交換市場近期定價的7月升息幅度約為9個基點，相當於升息25個基點的機率約36%；6月會議前，市場幾乎完全未反映這種可能性。涵蓋7月決策的8月聯邦資金期貨未平倉量，則由6月決議公布前約45.4萬口增加近30%，至週一收盤時接近59萬口。部位結構偏向可在緊縮預期升高時受益的空單，因此一旦就業或通膨數據轉弱，這項交易將特別容易反轉。

相同的拉鋸也出現在曲線較長端。摩根大通客戶調查顯示，美國公債淨部位為7個月來最偏多，投資人增加單純多頭部位之際，前端卻反映更多緊縮風險。自6月決策以來，2年與10年期利差在週三小幅陡峭化前已收窄約15個基點，反映市場焦點先前由勞動市場疑慮轉向通膨風險。Warsh較溫和的評估中斷了這股曲線趨平動能，但未扭轉實質殖利率更廣泛的升勢。

政策指引減少本身也可能影響美國公債估值。道明證券策略師認為，決策官員釋出的訊號減少，將迫使投資人在每次數據公布後重新評估政策路徑，從而提高市場波動與期限溢價。Warsh在6月首次主持FOMC會議以來，聯準會官員共公開露面12次，低於過去十年同期平均的18次。會議後債券波動仍相對穩定，因此預期中的影響尚未成為實際擾動；不過，溝通機制的轉變已開始改變投資人解讀不確定性的方式。

Warsh已指派前英格蘭銀行總裁Mervyn King共同主持溝通工作小組，檢討聯準會的溝通方式。King於2003年至2013年領導英格蘭銀行，先前也曾協助建立其通膨報告架構。這個溝通小組是Warsh成立的五個工作小組之一，其餘檢討範圍涵蓋資產負債表、資料運用、生產力與就業，以及通膨架構。各小組預計年底前提出結論；Warsh表示，包括美國以外人士在內的外部專家，最快下週就會公布。

Warsh也表示，他向來偏好規模較小的聯準會資產負債表，目前其規模約為$6.7兆；但他強調，任何變動都必須由FOMC決定，並公開討論。他指出，若要縮減至自己偏好的規模，需要超過18週。這番說法保留了政策利率以外的緊縮選項，卻沒有把縮表描述為迫在眉睫的行動。

當日美國數據也給了聯準會保留彈性的理由。ISM製造業指標維持在近4年高點附近，經濟活動連續第六個月擴張。包括印刷、電氣設備與紡織在內的14個產業呈現成長，紙製品、家具與木製品則萎縮。就業分項由48.6升至49.7，雖仍略低於50的門檻，但顯示工廠勞動市場的疲弱程度有所減輕。

物價壓力的緩和更為明顯。美國與伊朗達成暫時安排後，油價回落，ISM投入價格指標創下2022年7月以來最大單月跌幅。這樣的組合對債券相對有利：製造業動能仍在，戰爭帶來的最強烈成本壓力卻已消退。不過，產業擴張範圍廣泛，就業也在改善，持續顯示經濟具韌性，因此數據尚不足以帶動債券全面上漲。

6月民間就業同樣穩健增加，完成一年多來最強勁的3個月徵才期。資料未提供實際數值，但這項定性結果與ISM就業分項改善相呼應，並在政府就業報告公布前提供另一項勞動市場訊號。市場對聯準會7月政策的定價已容易受到徵才急劇轉弱的任何跡象影響，因此這項資料具有獨立意義。

紐約聯準銀行的HPW勞動市場緊俏指數，則對薪資提供較溫和的解讀。隨著離職人數及每名有效求職者所對應的職缺數小幅增加，這項研究指標由4月修正後的-0.07升至5月的-0.02。其數值相當於就業成本指數季增0.74%、年化成長2.96%，同時仍略低於標準化後的長期平均值。這不是紐約聯準銀行或FOMC的正式預測，但指標綜合離職、職缺及有效求職等面向後顯示，勞動市場不再像先前那樣快速降溫，卻也尚未指向薪資重新加速。

營建支出同樣偏弱，但並非衰退格局。5月總支出增加0.1%，經季節調整後年率達$2.2102兆，較一年前低1.5%。住宅營建較4月成長0.3%，公共建設增加0.5%，其中教育與公路支出均成長0.6%；民間非住宅營建則下降0.3%。1月至5月支出合計$8,584億，較2025年同期減少2.7%。這種組合顯示住宅與政府工程抵銷了企業相關建築的疲弱，而非資本支出全面加速。

季底交易激增後，美國公債現券市場活動大幅恢復正常。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.238兆，共420,852筆，較6月30日減少33.6%。名目附息債券交易量下降35.6%至$8,937億，TIPS交易量則減少60.5%至$269億。這些數字衡量雙向交易活動，無法顯示投資人方向，但可看出週三殖利率小幅上升時，季底的異常調整活動已經消退。

曲線前端又消化了一筆大型國庫券標售。美國財政部標售$720億、119天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.795%，投標倍數2.66倍，最高利率配售比例57.66%。競爭性投標總額為$1,900.95億，其中接受$703.80億；間接投標人獲配$388.38億，直接投標人獲配$46.73億，一級交易商獲配$268.69億。該券7月7日交割、11月3日到期，交割日與下一批4週及8週期國庫券標售相同。

## 歐洲通膨意外降溫，政策分歧擴大

隨著油價回落開始反映在區域物價數據中，歐元區6月通膨率由5月的3.2%降至2.8%，低於3%的預測中位數。核心通膨的降幅也超出預期，服務通膨則降至3.2%。數據公布後，德國10年期公債殖利率回吐早盤部分升幅；其間一度觸及2.90%，所報導的歐洲交易時段結束時上升2個基點至2.88%。

這項整體結果延續法國、德國與義大利先前公布的通膨降勢，也削弱ECB在6月升息後迅速再度行動的理由。伊朗戰爭及能源成本連續數月上漲，曾威脅讓通膨持續高於2%，ECB因而在上月將存款利率調升至2.25%，是2023年以來首次升息。如今油價已回到戰前水準，使ECB在6月採用的能源假設與當前市場走勢愈來愈不一致。

ECB總裁拉加德表示，短短幾週內，通膨上行風險與經濟成長下行風險已變得較為均衡。這項評估同時承認油價逆轉的速度及6月通膨轉弱，但不代表ECB會容忍通膨再度超標。改變的是風險的相對平衡及再次行動的急迫性，而非物價穩定目標。

管理委員會內部意見也因此更加分歧。希臘央行總裁Yannis Stournaras稱通膨降至2.8%是大幅低於預期的意外結果，並表示除非情勢劇烈改變，否則他預期7月不會調整利率。波斯灣地區央行官員先前曾向歐洲同行表示，能源基礎設施受損有限，大量伊朗原油可能重返市場；相較於先前對供應長期受阻的預期，這項判斷更為溫和。不過，Stournaras仍警告，企業可能迅速轉嫁能源價格上漲，卻未必會以相同速度將價格下跌反映給消費者。

拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks、斯洛維尼亞的Primoz Dolenc及芬蘭的Olli Rehn也認為7月沒有迫切行動的必要。Rehn表示，他不預期會出現重大的第二輪效應；奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher則稱，短期通膨威脅已經減弱。比利時的Pierre Wunsch指出，ECB甚至可能完全不需要再次升息。ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane及德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel仍保留選項，強調先前的能源漲價仍可能延後傳導至食品、服務及工資。

愛沙尼亞央行總裁Ulo Kaasik仍是最明確支持進一步緊縮的官員之一。他認為，油價衝擊後至少再升息一次似乎合理，並指出7月決策將取決於地緣政治，以及過去三個月商品價格上漲的傳導程度。他最主要的憂慮是通膨升高可能影響薪資協議，進而變得更為持久。Nagel同樣未排除7月或9月升息，即使他承認油價回落幅度令其意外。

市場定價介於兩派之間。貨幣市場仍認為9月前升息25個基點的機率超過50%，年底前升息一次的定價也接近完整反映；但市場對2026年內還會第二次升息的信心已下降。官員可以等待更多薪資與服務數據，7月不太可能爆發重大政策衝突；9月將有新預測出爐，屆時更可能成為分歧加劇的時點。

升息急迫性下降，不等於政策假設可直接回到戰前。歐元區通膨仍高於目標，服務價格仍以3.2%的速度上漲，多名官員也持續擔心薪資協議會納入先前的成本衝擊。新的資訊在於，現貨能源價格、整體通膨及核心指標都朝有利方向發展，使再次升息需要更充分的證據支持。

歐洲股市反映了部分壓力緩解，但並非毫無保留的風險偏好行情。Stoxx Europe 600指數下跌0.4%；官員表明不太可能急於行動後，指數自盤中更深跌幅回升。原油價格逼近每桶$71，能源股表現落後，公用事業與科技股也相對疲弱。歐洲銀行股在上一季上漲21%後進入當日交易，先前受到利率上升、交易及併購收入增加支撐；但通膨意外降溫，使市場不再能確信ECB繼續升息會持續支持銀行利潤率。

## AI融資擴張之際，困境債權人爭奪控制權

即使半導體股遭到拋售，科技融資週期仍持續擴張。截至5月，私募債發行額約達$810億，創2016年有統計以來同期新高；AI基礎設施借款人直接向保險公司及其他長期投資人籌集資金。這個市場已由規模較小、量身訂製的交易場所，發展為足以吸收數十億美元融資的市場。

經營AI模型訓練資料中心的IREN於5月透過私募籌得約$21億。Blackstone支持的QTS先前已籌得$8億，並考慮進一步舉債。Broadcom與Anthropic的融資案總額達$350億；交易最初採傳統私募形式，但預期最終將依Rule 144A在更廣泛的市場交易。

這類結構讓日益增加的保險負債與長天期公司資產相互搭配。美國去年年金銷售額創下約$4,640億的紀錄，提高了保險公司對高評等債券的需求，以支應未來數十年的給付。私募債流動性較低，因此相對公開市場證券提供額外殖利率；借款人在幣別、期限、規模、評等及資訊揭露方面則享有較大彈性。

這種配置也伴隨風險。相關債務較難追蹤；當公開市場的AI相關債券已經波動時，流動性有限的影響會更加顯著。投資人必須判斷，在整段債務存續期間，資料中心與運算資產是否仍能持續產生經濟效益。去年私募案平均規模為$3.53億，平均期限9.5年；如今主辦機構收到的單筆融資需求已達$20億至$30億以上。

半導體股賣壓凸顯了這項疑問，但並未造成廣泛的信用市場重挫。費城半導體指數下跌6.27%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.54%；LQD下跌0.56%，HYG下跌0.48%，JNK下跌0.51%。這些基金價格也受到政府公債殖利率上升影響，無法單獨反映信用利差表現，但其跌勢顯示固定收益風險資產也未能避開科技股疲弱的交易日。

企業融資需求也可能獲得近年來最強勁上半年併購活動的支持。全球交易金額較一年前增加約30%至$2.6兆，企業共宣布38筆金額至少$100億的交易，為任何半年期間之最。這些活動提高了下半年併購融資及過橋貸款再融資的可能性；不過，借款成本偏高，加上部分投資是在先前估值更昂貴時完成，私募股權退出活動仍受到壓抑。

個別發行人的信用壓力遠比廣泛基金跌勢嚴重。Trans-Oil一筆2031年到期、規模$3億的債券，較週二開盤下跌約21美分後，報價接近面額每1美元70美分；另一筆2029年到期、規模$4.5億的債券，報價同樣約為70美分。烏克蘭媒體報導指稱，創辦人Vaja Jhashi參與一項涉及向伊朗運送穀物、違反制裁的安排後，這家穀物與油籽公司安排於週四召開全球投資人電話會議。

Trans-Oil與Jhashi斷然否認相關指控，並聘請Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman進行調查。該報導本身並未點名Trans-Oil，ING信用分析師Egor Fedorov也預期，事件對公司基本面的影響有限。債券價格的反應仍顯示，治理與制裁疑慮可能迅速壓過一般營運分析，對仰賴烏克蘭採購及區域物流的發行人尤其如此。

Brightline面臨的是另一種困境。債權人正著手重整其$55億債務，卻尚未就由誰主導程序達成協議。這家佛州私營鐵路業者擁有足夠準備金，可支付7月1日公司債及優先順位市政債的票息；但這些準備金預計是公司最後一項可直接動用、避免正式違約的手段。

至少三個債權人團體正在競相提供破產融資。持有Brightline $12億公司債多數部位的避險基金準備否決任何無法讓其取得控制權的交易。為$11億免稅債券提供保險的Assured Guaranty，已經提供臨時營運貸款。包括Nuveen、Invesco與First Eagle在內的市政債投資人，則在考慮提供超優先順位融資，使其可能取得所有權。

債權人團體先前一直設法讓列車營運單位留在破產程序之外，部分原因是避免適用必須設置獨立受託人的特殊程序。Fortress Investment Group願意放棄控制權，但貸款人仍未就可限制法院程序成本及時間的方案達成一致。Brightline佛州路線未能達到先前預測，同時又承諾投入擬議中的$215億Brightline West計畫，因此債權人協商的不只是回收價值，還包括一條營運中鐵路的控制權及其未來資本需求。

## 美元走強，再度凸顯亞洲匯率與政策矛盾

美國實質殖利率處於高檔，聯準會仍有升息風險，兩者的影響壓過Warsh較溫和的通膨評估，帶動美元上漲。美元指數上升0.20%至101.39，月線漲幅達2.51%。新興市場貨幣下跌0.2%，抹去2026年以來的整體漲幅，MSCI貨幣指數則逼近4月7日以來最低收盤水準。

亞洲貨幣領跌。外資淨賣出1.46兆韓元、約合$9.38億的韓國股票，韓元因而逼近2009年以來最低水準。先前人民幣升值交易的動能也已消退。聯準會6月決策後，大額美元兌人民幣買權交易比賣權活躍，一個月期選擇權偏斜轉向防範美元走強。花旗估計，投資人大致已平倉美元兌人民幣空單，使整體部位更接近中性。

日圓仍是最棘手的政策問題。儘管日本央行6月將政策利率升至1%，創1995年以來最高，日圓仍在一美元兌162.73日圓附近交易，接近1986年低點。避險基金建立了2017年以來最大規模的日圓空頭部位；選擇權市場顯示，美元兌日圓一年內升至180的機率為15%。升至200的機率不到1%，但部分投資人認為，如果美國通膨重新升高、美國公債殖利率上升、油價變貴且日本央行延後政策正常化等極端情況同時發生，仍有可能觸及該水準。

日本當局已在4月28日至5月27日期間動用創紀錄的¥11.73兆支撐日圓。財務省國際事務次官Atsushi Mimura表示，這項讓日圓升向155的操作相當成功，也獲得美國支持。日圓後來再度走弱，顯示干預並未改變根本的利差與財政疑慮。日本政府債務超過GDP的200%；市場預期財政政策將趨於擴張，加上要求日本央行漸進緊縮的壓力，降低了投資人對國內政策能迅速縮小殖利率差距的信心。

日本央行6月貨幣基數數據在美國固定收益市場收盤後、後續亞洲時段公布，量化呈現央行持續收回流動性的情況。貨幣基數較一年前萎縮13.7%，快於5月的12.2%降幅；日本央行經常帳戶餘額下降16.4%，準備金餘額減少14.6%，經季節調整的月度年化萎縮率則由13.3%加快至22.9%。平均貨幣基數餘額由¥575.763兆降至¥559.204兆。資產負債表正常化仍未阻止日圓走弱，因投資人持續聚焦於日本與其他國家的相對升息速度及日本財政前景。

同樣在美國收盤後公布的韓國通膨數據，則提高了另一家亞洲央行維持鷹派立場的壓力。6月消費者物價較一年前上漲3.2%，符合預測中位數，並高於5月的3.1%；核心通膨維持2.5%。交通價格上漲11.1%，休閒與文化價格增加5.4%，顯示基礎通膨壓力仍具韌性之際，整體物價也持續受到能源影響。

韓國央行將於7月16日開會；上次會議已有兩名決策官員主張立即升息。總裁Shin Hyun Song曾警告，半導體榮景正擴散至消費、工資與投資。6月半導體出貨量接近增為三倍，帶動按工作日調整的出口成長率升至近60%；政府同時協調企業對晶片廠及AI資料中心進行至少1,350兆韓元的投資。出口強勁、韓元疲弱、房價偏高及核心通膨持續存在，使政策焦點不再是理事會是否需要考慮緊縮，而是何時行動。

能源仍是上述匯率與政策走勢的共同變數。截至6月26日當週，美國商業原油庫存減少380萬桶至4.084億桶，汽油庫存下降230萬桶，餾分油庫存增加250萬桶。煉油廠產能利用率由96.1%升至96.6%，原油投入量增至每日1,719.6萬桶；國內產量則維持每日1,381萬桶。

戰略石油儲備減少550萬桶至3.257億桶，使整體庫存狀況不像期貨價格下跌所顯示的那樣全面寬鬆。不過，美國與伊朗接觸改善及區域出口恢復仍主導市場價格。阿拉伯聯合大公國6月原油與凝析油出口增加約30%，至每日逾390萬桶，接近2017年有統計以來最高水準。高盛預期，戰爭造成的干擾逐漸消退，加上荷莫茲海峽運輸恢復，明年石油供給過剩幅度平均將略高於每日300萬桶，戰略儲備採購則會抵銷部分過剩。

## 後續市場意義

因假期提前公布的美國就業報告，是利率市場下一項直接考驗，將於7月2日美東時間08:30與截至6月27日當週的初領失業救濟金人數同步公布。市場預期雇主6月增加11.5萬名員工；若符合預期，將構成2024年年中以來最強勁的6個月徵才表現。市場將把結果與穩健的民間就業、ISM就業分項改善及HPW指數溫和回升相互比對。薪資、失業率及徵才廣度都很重要，因市場已圍繞7月可能升息累積聯邦資金利率空單，而Warsh取消了原本可能抑制市場反應的慣常指引。

5月工廠訂單將於美東時間10:00公布。民間非住宅營建在5月下降後，這項數據將協助判斷製造業連續第六個月擴張是否正轉化為持久需求。訂單展現韌性且就業穩健，將保留聯準會緊縮選項；若數據廣泛惡化，則會挑戰投入成本已經轉弱、實質殖利率卻仍維持升勢的市場格局。

美國財政部將於美東時間11:30分別標售$850億的4週及8週期國庫券。28天期與56天期券都在7月7日交割，與週三售出的$720億、119天期國庫券相同。合計$1,700億的供給，將在獨立紀念日休市前測試集中交割日的現金需求。SIFMA建議美國固定收益市場於7月2日美東時間14:00收盤，使市場必須在縮短的交易時段內消化就業、初領失業救濟金、工廠訂單及國庫券供給。

美國固定收益市場7月3日休市。紐約聯準銀行第二季工作人員即時預測預定於休市期間的美東時間12:45發布，因此將成為一項沒有同日美國公債完整收盤可供觀察的經濟更新。市場恢復交易後，6月ISM服務業指數及紐約聯準銀行全球供應鏈壓力指數將於7月6日美東時間10:00公布。服務價格與物流壓力將顯示，製造業投入成本的改善是否已擴展至規模更大、勞力更密集的服務業。

歐洲下一批數據包括7月2日美東時間02:30公布的瑞士6月通膨，以及05:00公布的歐元區5月失業率。歐元區通膨已降至2.8%；這些數據將進一步釐清主張可以暫停行動的官員，與擔心薪資及延後出現第二輪效應的官員之間的分歧。若沒有新的衝擊，ECB不太可能在7月再次升息；但服務通膨、勞動市場閒置程度及秋季薪資協議，仍可能重新建立9月升息的理由。

油價仍是聯準會、ECB及亞洲貨幣前景共同的關鍵條件。荷莫茲海峽運輸持續、美國與伊朗朝正式協議邁進且出口保持穩定，將強化損益兩平通膨率的降勢，並降低歐洲進一步緊縮的急迫性。若攻擊再起、出口基礎設施受損或談判破裂，這些利多就會逆轉；日本與韓國尤其脆弱，因匯率疲弱會放大進口能源成本。

下一項較長期的美國政策訊號，是7月8日公布的6月16日至17日FOMC會議紀要。投資人將關注3.50%至3.75%目標區間、利率預測各半，以及減少前瞻指引等決定背後的討論。會議紀要可釐清多少官員認同Warsh所稱通膨風險已下降的看法、2026年稍晚升息獲得多少支持，以及資產負債表或充裕準備金相關問題是否正在接近實際政策決定。

overall_summary.headline: 美國經濟活動具韌性，實質殖利率維持高檔，公債曲線轉趨陡峭
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債在紐約正常交易時段收盤時，前端變動不大，較長天期債券則溫和走弱。2年期殖利率上升0.2個基點至4.177%，10年期上升1.4個基點至4.48%，30年期上升1.8個基點至4.971%。10年期實質殖利率上升1.7個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降0.3個基點，顯示賣壓源自實質利率偏高，而非通膨衝擊再起。

Warsh表示，過去四週通膨預期與風險均已下降，一度帶動2年期殖利率回落至約4.15%，但他拒絕為7月決策提供指引。製造業連續第六個月擴張，民間徵才依然穩健，抵銷ISM投入價格創2022年7月以來最大單月跌幅的影響。美國與伊朗接觸改善也帶動油價下跌，進一步強化近期通膨壓力轉弱的訊號。

半導體股重挫6.27%，卻未引發資金全面湧入美國公債避險；美元走強，上市信用債基金則下跌。歐元區通膨降至低於預期的2.8%，降低ECB再次升息的急迫性。與此同時，AI相關私募融資持續擴張，Trans-Oil與Brightline則顯現嚴重的個別發行人壓力。
overall_summary.summary: Warsh對通膨的評估轉趨溫和，加上油價下跌，降低了7月升息的急迫性；但製造業與徵才仍然穩健，使美國長天期公債殖利率承壓，前端則幾乎沒有變化。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries finished July 1 little changed at the front end but modestly weaker in longer maturities, as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s acknowledgment that inflation risks had declined competed with resilient U.S. manufacturing and hiring evidence. The 2-year yield rose 0.2 basis point to 4.177%, the 5-year increased 1.1 basis points to 4.238%, the 10-year climbed 1.4 basis points to 4.48% and the 30-year added 1.8 basis points to 4.971%. The curve steepened slightly, with 2s10s widening 1.2 basis points to 30.3 basis points and 2s30s increasing 1.6 basis points to 79.4 basis points.

The modest selloff was concentrated in real rates rather than inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield rose 1.7 basis points to 2.243%, while the 10-year breakeven rate slipped 0.3 basis point to 2.237%. That composition was consistent with an economy still expanding and a Fed unwilling to pre-commit, even as lower oil and easing input costs reduced the immediate inflation threat. Warsh said inflation expectations and risks had come down over the preceding four weeks, briefly pulling the 2-year yield to about 4.15%, but he refused to indicate whether a July increase remained under consideration.

Manufacturing expanded for a sixth consecutive month, and private-sector employment recorded another solid increase. The Institute for Supply Management’s prices measure posted its largest monthly decline since July 2022, however, while the employment component improved but remained just below the expansion threshold. A New York Fed labor-tightness indicator also suggested wage growth close to, though slightly below, its long-run norm. Together, the releases supported continued growth without restoring the more acute inflation signal that had driven rate-increase expectations after the Fed’s June meeting.

Energy reinforced that distinction. WTI fell 1.32% to $68.58 and Brent declined 1.85% to $71.57 after U.S. officials described indirect discussions with Iran as constructive. Commercial crude and gasoline inventories fell, but the decline in market prices and a distillate-stock increase kept the inflation signal contained. The 1-month losses in WTI and Brent exceeded 21%, a reversal large enough to matter for headline inflation and central-bank assumptions even though the durability of the U.S.-Iran arrangement remains uncertain.

Risk markets did not produce the usual clean counterpart to the rates move. The S&P 500 slipped 0.22%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.54% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 6.27%. Treasuries nevertheless failed to rally, showing that the chip selloff did not become a broad flight to safety. The dollar index rose 0.20% to 101.39, while listed investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds all declined. The day’s defining feature was therefore not a renewed inflation shock or a generalized credit event, but the persistence of elevated real yields as investors balanced softer price signals against resilient activity, reduced Fed guidance and a growing supply of capital-intensive technology debt.

## Warsh Lowers the Inflation Temperature Without Guiding July

Warsh’s Sintra appearance reduced the urgency around a July increase without resolving the policy decision. He said inflation expectations and inflation risks had declined in recent weeks and repeated the Fed’s commitment to returning inflation to 2%. The market response was clearest in the policy-sensitive sector: the 2-year Treasury yield fell to its session low near 4.15% after the remarks before ending the date close at 4.177%, almost unchanged from the previous session.

The chair did not identify the price indicators behind his assessment. The latest annual increase in the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge was 4.1%, with the core measure at 3.4%, but oil and gasoline prices had fallen sharply as peace efforts between the U.S. and Iran progressed. His comments therefore recognized an important improvement in the near-term inflation environment without declaring that broader price pressure had returned to target.

Warsh also declined to say whether an increase was on the table for the July 28-29 meeting. He reiterated that the Fed would stop providing the kind of forward guidance that commits markets to an expected rate path and said policymakers would have a substantive debate when they meet. The FOMC unanimously maintained the federal funds target at 3.50%-3.75% in June, while half of the 18 officials who submitted projections expected a rate increase during 2026. Warsh was the only official not to submit a rate forecast.

That communication shift leaves incoming releases with greater capacity to move the front end. Interest-rate swaps had recently priced about 9 basis points of a quarter-point July increase, roughly a 36% probability, up from almost nothing before the June meeting. Open interest in August federal funds futures, which cover the July decision, had risen almost 30% from about 454,000 contracts before the June announcement to nearly 590,000 by Monday’s close. The buildup was skewed toward short positions that benefit if tightening expectations increase, making the trade vulnerable to weaker employment or inflation evidence.

The same tension was visible farther along the curve. A JPMorgan client survey showed net Treasury positioning at its most bullish in 7 months, with investors adding outright longs even as the front end priced more tightening risk. The 2s10s curve had narrowed about 15 basis points since the June decision before Wednesday’s slight steepening, reflecting the earlier shift from labor-market concern toward inflation risk. Warsh’s softer assessment interrupted that flattening impulse but did not reverse the broader increase in real yields.

Less guidance may itself affect Treasury valuation. TD Securities strategists argued that fewer signals from policymakers could increase market volatility and term premium by forcing investors to reassess the path after each data release. Fed officials had made 12 public appearances since Warsh’s June FOMC debut, compared with an average of 18 over the comparable period during the previous decade. Bond volatility had remained relatively stable since the meeting, so the anticipated effect had not yet become a realized disruption, but the communication regime is already changing how investors interpret uncertainty.

Warsh has assigned former Bank of England Governor Mervyn King to co-chair a communications task force that will review the Fed’s approach. King led the BOE from 2003 through 2013 and previously helped shape its inflation-report framework. The communications group is one of five task forces Warsh created to examine the balance sheet, data use, productivity and employment, inflation frameworks and public messaging. Their conclusions are expected by year-end, and Warsh said outside experts, including some from outside the U.S., would be announced as early as next week.

The chair also said he has historically favored a smaller Fed balance sheet, now about $6.7 trillion, while emphasizing that any change would be an FOMC decision and would be deliberated publicly. He said a reduction to his preferred size would take more than 18 weeks. That preserved a tightening option beyond the policy rate without presenting balance-sheet action as imminent.

The day’s U.S. releases gave the Fed reason to retain flexibility. The ISM manufacturing gauge remained near a 4-year high as activity expanded for a sixth consecutive month. Fourteen industries, including printing, electrical equipment and textiles, reported growth; paper products, furniture and wood products contracted. The employment subindex rose to 49.7 from 48.6, still marginally below the 50 threshold but consistent with less severe factory-labor weakness.

Price pressure eased more visibly. ISM’s input-price measure recorded its largest monthly decline since July 2022 as oil retreated following the interim U.S.-Iran agreement. The combination was comparatively favorable for bonds: manufacturing retained momentum, but the most acute war-driven cost pressure receded. It was not weak enough to generate a duration rally because the breadth of industrial expansion and improving employment still pointed to economic resilience.

Private-sector employment also increased solidly in June, completing the strongest 3-month hiring stretch in more than a year. No numerical actual was supplied, but the qualitative result reinforced the ISM employment improvement and preceded the government payroll report. The evidence mattered as a distinct labor signal because the Fed’s July pricing had become exposed to any indication that hiring was weakening sharply.

The New York Fed’s HPW Labor Market Tightness Index added a more moderate wage reading. The research measure rose to -0.02 in May from a revised -0.07 in April as quits and vacancies per effective job searcher increased modestly. It was consistent with 0.74% quarterly growth in the Employment Cost Index, or 2.96% annualized, while remaining slightly below its normalized long-run mean. The measure is not an official New York Fed or FOMC forecast, but its breadth across quits, vacancies and effective search suggested labor conditions were no longer loosening as rapidly without yet pointing to renewed wage acceleration.

Construction spending was similarly subdued rather than recessionary. Total outlays increased 0.1% in May to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $2.2102 trillion, 1.5% below a year earlier. Residential construction rose 0.3% from April and public construction gained 0.5%, including 0.6% increases in educational and highway spending. Private nonresidential construction fell 0.3%. Spending during January through May totaled $858.4 billion, down 2.7% from the same period in 2025. The composition showed housing and government projects offsetting weakness in business-related building rather than a broad capital-spending acceleration.

Treasury cash activity normalized sharply after the quarter-end surge. FINRA recorded $1.238 trillion of par trading across 420,852 transactions, down 33.6% from June 30. Nominal-coupon activity fell 35.6% to $893.7 billion, while TIPS turnover declined 60.5% to $26.9 billion. The figures measure two-way activity, not investor direction, but they show that Wednesday’s small yield increases occurred as the exceptional quarter-end adjustment subsided.

The front end absorbed another large bill sale. Treasury’s $72 billion 119-day auction stopped at a 3.795% high rate, with a 2.66 bid-to-cover ratio and 57.66% allotted at the high. Competitive tenders totaled $190.095 billion, of which $70.380 billion was accepted. Indirect bidders received $38.838 billion, direct bidders $4.673 billion and primary dealers $26.869 billion. The security settles July 7 and matures November 3, placing its cash date alongside the next 4- and 8-week bill auctions.

## Europe’s Inflation Surprise Opens a Wider Policy Divide

Euro-area inflation slowed to 2.8% in June from 3.2% in May, below the 3% median forecast, as the retreat in oil began to appear in the regional price data. Core inflation also eased more than expected, and services inflation fell to 3.2%. German 10-year yields pared an earlier rise after the release, ending the reported European session 2 basis points higher at 2.88% after touching 2.90%.

The aggregate result extended the national declines reported across France, Germany and Italy and weakened the case for rapidly following the ECB’s June increase with another move. The ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.25% last month, its first increase since 2023, after the Iran war and several months of higher energy costs threatened to keep inflation above 2%. Oil has since returned to pre-war levels, leaving the institution’s June energy assumptions increasingly out of line with current markets.

President Christine Lagarde said upside inflation risk and downside growth risk had become more broadly balanced within only a few weeks. Her assessment recognized both the speed of the oil reversal and the softer June inflation result without suggesting that the ECB would tolerate a renewed overshoot. The change was in the balance of risks and the urgency of another move, not in the price-stability objective.

The Governing Council’s internal range widened accordingly. Greek central-bank Governor Yannis Stournaras described the decline to 2.8% as a large downside surprise and said he expected no move in July unless conditions changed dramatically. Gulf central bankers had told their European counterparts that damage to energy infrastructure was limited and that substantial Iranian oil could return to the market, a more benign assessment than earlier expectations of prolonged disruption. Stournaras still warned that firms may pass energy increases through quickly while failing to transmit price declines at the same speed.

Latvia’s Martins Kazaks, Slovenia’s Primoz Dolenc and Finland’s Olli Rehn also saw little urgency for July. Rehn said he did not expect major second-round effects, while Austrian Governor Martin Kocher said the inflation threat had diminished in the short term. Belgium’s Pierre Wunsch indicated that another increase might not be necessary at all. Chief Economist Philip Lane and Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel kept their options open, emphasizing the possibility that earlier energy increases could still reach food, services and wages with a delay.

Estonian Governor Ulo Kaasik remained among the clearest advocates of further tightening. He said at least one more increase appeared reasonable after the oil shock and identified the July decision as dependent on both geopolitics and the pass-through from the preceding 3 months of commodity-price increases. His principal concern was that higher inflation could influence wage agreements and become more persistent. Nagel likewise kept both July and September open, even while acknowledging that the size of oil’s retreat had surprised him.

Market pricing moved between those camps. Money markets continued to assign a greater than 50% chance to a 25-basis-point increase by September and came close to pricing a full move by year-end, but doubts about a second increase during 2026 had grown. July appeared unlikely to produce a major confrontation because officials could wait for additional wage and services data; September, when new forecasts are available, is the more likely point for the disagreement to sharpen.

The reduced urgency did not amount to a simple return to pre-war policy assumptions. Euro-area inflation remained above target, services were still rising at 3.2%, and several officials continued to worry that wage agreements would incorporate the earlier cost shock. The new information was that spot energy, headline inflation and core measures had all moved in the same favorable direction, raising the evidentiary burden for another increase.

European equities reflected that partial relief but not an unqualified risk rally. The Stoxx Europe 600 fell 0.4%, recovering from deeper session losses as officials indicated they were unlikely to rush. Energy stocks lagged as crude moved toward $71 a barrel, while utilities and technology also underperformed. European banks entered the session after a 21% quarterly gain, supported by higher rates and stronger trading and dealmaking revenue, but the inflation surprise reduced the certainty that further ECB increases would continue supporting margins.

## AI Financing Expands as Distressed Credits Fight Over Control

The technology financing cycle continued to grow even as semiconductor equities sold off. Private bond issuance reached roughly $81 billion through May, the largest total for that period in data extending to 2016, as artificial-intelligence infrastructure borrowers sought capital directly from insurance companies and other long-horizon investors. The market has expanded from a venue for smaller, bespoke transactions into one capable of absorbing multi-billion-dollar financings.

IREN, which operates data centers used to train AI models, raised about $2.1 billion through a private placement in May. Blackstone-backed QTS had previously raised $800 million and was considering additional borrowing. A financing package for Broadcom and Anthropic totaled $35 billion; it began as a traditional private placement but is expected eventually to trade more broadly under Rule 144A.

The structure matches a growing pool of insurance liabilities with long-duration corporate assets. U.S. annuity sales reached a record of about $464 billion last year, increasing insurers’ need for high-grade bonds capable of backing payments over several decades. Private placements offer additional yield over public securities because they are less liquid, while borrowers receive greater flexibility over currency, maturity, size, ratings and disclosure.

That balance also carries risks. The debt can be harder to track, and limited liquidity becomes more consequential when public AI-related bonds are already volatile. Investors must assess whether data centers and computing assets will remain economically productive for as long as the debt remains outstanding. Average private-placement size was $353 million last year with a 9.5-year maturity, but arrangers are now receiving requests for single financings of $2 billion to $3 billion or more.

The semiconductor selloff sharpened that question without creating a broad credit break. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 6.27%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.54%. LQD declined 0.56%, HYG lost 0.48% and JNK fell 0.51%. Those fund prices were also affected by the rise in government yields and do not by themselves isolate spread performance, but their declines showed that fixed-income risk assets did not escape the weaker technology session.

Corporate financing demand may also receive support from the strongest first half for mergers and acquisitions in several years. Global transaction value increased about 30% from a year earlier to $2.6 trillion, and companies announced 38 deals worth at least $10 billion, the largest number for any 6-month period. The activity raises the prospect of acquisition financing and bridge takeouts during the second half, even though private-equity exits remain restrained by higher borrowing costs and investments made at earlier, richer valuations.

Issuer-level credit stress was much more severe than the broad fund moves. Trans-Oil’s $300 million bond due in 2031 was quoted near 70 cents on the dollar after falling about 21 cents from Tuesday’s open. A separate $450 million issue due in 2029 was also quoted around 70. The grain and oilseed company scheduled a global investor call for Thursday after a Ukrainian media report alleged that founder Vaja Jhashi participated in a sanctions-violating scheme involving grain shipments to Iran.

Trans-Oil and Jhashi categorically rejected the allegations and retained Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman to investigate. The report did not name Trans-Oil itself, and ING credit analyst Egor Fedorov expected only limited impact on the company’s fundamentals. The bond reaction nevertheless showed how quickly governance and sanctions concerns can overwhelm ordinary operating analysis, particularly for an issuer exposed to Ukrainian sourcing and regional logistics.

Brightline faced a different form of distress as creditors approached a restructuring of its $5.5 billion debt load without agreement on who would control the process. The private Florida railroad had sufficient reserves to make July 1 coupon payments on its corporate and senior municipal bonds, but those reserves were expected to represent its last straightforward means of avoiding formal default.

At least three creditor groups were competing to provide bankruptcy financing. Hedge funds holding a majority of Brightline’s $1.2 billion of corporate debt were prepared to reject a transaction that did not give them control. Assured Guaranty, which insures $1.1 billion of tax-exempt bonds, had provided interim operating loans. Municipal investors including Nuveen, Invesco and First Eagle were considering super-senior financing that could position them to take ownership.

The creditor groups had previously sought to keep the train-operating unit outside bankruptcy, partly to avoid special procedures requiring an independent trustee. Fortress Investment Group was prepared to relinquish control, but lenders had not agreed on a plan that would limit the cost and duration of a court process. Brightline’s inability to meet earlier projections on its Florida route and its parallel commitment to the proposed $21.5 billion Brightline West project left creditors negotiating not merely over recovery values, but over control of an operating railroad and its future capital requirements.

## Dollar Strength Reopens Asia’s Currency and Policy Fault Lines

The dollar gained as the combination of elevated U.S. real yields and residual Fed tightening risk outweighed Warsh’s softer inflation assessment. The U.S. Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 101.39 and was 2.51% higher over the month. Emerging-market currencies fell 0.2%, erasing their aggregate 2026 gain and taking the MSCI currency index toward its weakest close since April 7.

Asian currencies led the decline. The South Korean won approached its weakest level since 2009 as foreign investors sold a net 1.46 trillion won, or $938 million, of Korean equities. The yuan’s earlier appreciation trade also lost momentum. Since the Fed’s June decision, large dollar-yuan call options had traded more heavily than puts, and the 1-month skew shifted toward protection against dollar strength. Citigroup estimated that investors had largely closed short dollar-yuan positions, leaving positioning closer to neutral.

The yen remained the most acute policy problem. It traded around 162.73 per dollar, near a 1986 low, despite the Bank of Japan’s June increase to 1%, its highest policy rate since 1995. Hedge funds had built their largest bearish yen position since 2017, while options markets assigned a 15% chance to dollar-yen reaching 180 within a year. The probability of 200 was less than 1%, although some investors regarded that level as possible under an extreme combination of renewed U.S. inflation, higher Treasury yields, more expensive oil and delayed BOJ normalization.

Japanese authorities had already spent a record ¥11.73 trillion from April 28 through May 27 supporting the currency. Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Atsushi Mimura said that operation, which strengthened the yen toward 155, had been successful and enjoyed U.S. support. The subsequent reversal showed that intervention had not changed the underlying rate differential or fiscal concerns. Japan’s government debt exceeds 200% of GDP, while expectations of expansionary fiscal policy and pressure for gradual BOJ tightening have reduced confidence that domestic policy will narrow the yield gap quickly.

The BOJ’s June monetary-base data, released later in the Asia-to-Asia window after the completed U.S. fixed-income close, quantified the ongoing withdrawal of central-bank liquidity. The monetary base contracted 13.7% from a year earlier, faster than May’s 12.2% decline. BOJ current-account balances fell 16.4%, reserve balances declined 14.6% and the seasonally adjusted monthly rate of contraction accelerated to 22.9% annualized from 13.3%. The average monetary-base balance decreased to ¥559.204 trillion from ¥575.763 trillion. That balance-sheet normalization did not prevent currency weakness because investors remained focused on the relative pace of rate increases and Japan’s fiscal outlook.

South Korea’s inflation release, also arriving after the U.S. close, added pressure for another Asian central bank to maintain a hawkish stance. Consumer prices rose 3.2% from a year earlier in June, matching the median forecast and accelerating from 3.1% in May. Core inflation held at 2.5%. Transportation prices increased 11.1%, while recreation and culture rose 5.4%, keeping the headline exposed to energy even as underlying pressure remained resilient.

The Bank of Korea meets on July 16 after two policymakers had already favored an immediate rate increase at the previous meeting. Governor Shin Hyun Song has warned that the semiconductor boom is spreading into consumption, wages and investment. Semiconductor shipments nearly tripled in June, helping lift working-day-adjusted export growth to almost 60%, while the government is coordinating at least 1,350 trillion won of corporate investment in chip plants and AI data centers. The combination of strong exports, a weak won, elevated housing prices and persistent core inflation makes the timing of tightening the central question rather than whether the board will need to consider it.

Energy remained a common qualification across those currency and policy developments. U.S. commercial crude inventories fell 3.8 million barrels in the week ended June 26 to 408.4 million, while gasoline stocks declined 2.3 million and distillates increased 2.5 million. Refinery utilization rose to 96.6% from 96.1%, and crude inputs increased to 17.196 million barrels a day. Domestic production held at 13.810 million barrels a day.

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by 5.5 million barrels to 325.7 million, making the inventory picture less uniformly comfortable than the drop in futures implied. Yet improving U.S.-Iran contacts and restored regional exports dominated market prices. The United Arab Emirates increased crude and condensate shipments by roughly 30% during June to more than 3.9 million barrels a day, close to the highest level in data extending to 2017. Goldman Sachs expected the fading war disruption and recovering Hormuz traffic to produce an oil surplus averaging slightly more than 3 million barrels a day next year, partially offset by purchases for strategic reserves.

## Forward Market Significance

The holiday-advanced U.S. employment report is the immediate rates test at 08:30 ET on July 2, alongside initial claims for the week ended June 27. Employers are expected to have added 115,000 jobs in June, which would complete the strongest 6-month hiring stretch since mid-2024. The result will be assessed against solid private-sector hiring, the improvement in ISM employment and the HPW index’s modest rebound. Wages, unemployment and the breadth of hiring will matter because short federal funds positions have accumulated around a possible July increase, while Warsh has removed the usual guidance that might otherwise damp the market response.

May factory orders follow at 10:00 ET. The release will help determine whether manufacturing’s sixth month of expansion is being converted into durable demand after private nonresidential construction fell in May. A resilient orders profile alongside firm employment would preserve the Fed’s option to tighten; a broad deterioration would challenge the real-yield increase that remained in place despite softer input costs.

Treasury auctions $85 billion each of 4- and 8-week bills at 11:30 ET. The 28-day and 56-day securities settle July 7, the same date as the $72 billion 119-day bill sold Wednesday. The combined $170 billion offering will test cash demand across a concentrated settlement date immediately before the Independence Day interruption. The SIFMA-recommended fixed-income close is 14:00 ET on July 2, compressing the market’s response to payrolls, claims, factory orders and bill supply into a shortened session.

U.S. fixed-income markets are closed July 3. The New York Fed’s second-quarter staff nowcast is scheduled for 12:45 ET during that closure, making it an economic update without a same-day completed Treasury close. Trading resumes with June ISM services and the New York Fed’s Global Supply Chain Pressure Index at 10:00 ET on July 6. Services prices and logistics pressure will show whether the improvement visible in manufacturing inputs extends to the larger, more labor-intensive part of the economy.

Europe’s next evidence arrives with Swiss June inflation at 02:30 ET and euro-area May unemployment at 05:00 on July 2. The releases follow the decline in euro-area inflation to 2.8% and will refine the dispute between officials who see room to pause and those concerned about wages and delayed second-round effects. The July ECB decision appears unlikely to deliver another increase without a renewed shock, but services inflation, labor slack and autumn wage agreements remain capable of restoring the September case.

Oil is still the shared condition across the Fed, ECB and Asian currency outlooks. Continued Hormuz traffic, progress toward a formal U.S.-Iran agreement and sustained exports would reinforce the decline in breakeven inflation and reduce the urgency of additional European tightening. Renewed attacks, damage to export infrastructure or a breakdown in talks would reverse that relief, particularly for Japan and South Korea, where weak currencies amplify imported energy costs.

The next longer-horizon U.S. policy signal is the July 8 release of minutes from the June 16-17 FOMC meeting. Investors will look for the discussion behind the 3.50%-3.75% target range, the evenly divided rate projections and the decision to reduce forward guidance. The minutes can clarify how broadly officials share Warsh’s view that inflation risks have declined, how much support exists for increases later in 2026 and whether balance-sheet or ample-reserves questions are moving closer to an operational decision.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve steepens as resilient U.S. activity keeps real yields elevated
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended the regular NY session little changed at the front end and modestly weaker in longer maturities. The 2-year yield rose 0.2 basis point to 4.177%, while the 10-year climbed 1.4 basis points to 4.48% and the 30-year added 1.8 basis points to 4.971%. The 10-year real yield increased 1.7 basis points as its breakeven rate slipped 0.3 basis point, showing that the selloff reflected elevated real rates rather than a renewed inflation shock.

Warsh said inflation expectations and risks had declined over the preceding four weeks, briefly pulling the 2-year yield toward 4.15%, but he declined to guide the July decision. Manufacturing expanded for a sixth month and private hiring remained solid, offsetting the largest monthly decline in ISM input prices since July 2022. Oil also fell as U.S.-Iran contacts improved, reinforcing the softer near-term inflation signal.

A 6.27% semiconductor selloff did not generate a broad flight into Treasuries, while the dollar strengthened and listed credit funds declined. Euro-area inflation slowed more than expected to 2.8%, reducing the urgency of another ECB increase. Meanwhile, private AI-related financing continued to expand even as Trans-Oil and Brightline showed severe issuer-specific stress.
overall_summary.summary: Warsh’s softer inflation assessment and lower oil reduced the urgency of a July rate increase, but solid manufacturing and hiring kept longer Treasury yields under pressure and left the front end nearly unchanged.
